newsitem.title: USA: Ontario Hydro to shut Pickering nukes in December.
newsitem.headline: Ontario Hydro to shut Pickering nukes in December.

text.p: Ontario Hydro planned to close its four 500 MW megawatt (MW) Pickering A nuclear power units at the end of December and three 800 MW Bruce A units at the end of March 1998, a company spokesman said Thursday.

On Wednesday, the provincially owned utility announced a temporary shutdown of those units to upgrade and extensively overhaul its beleaguered nuclear operations, an undertaking which could cost C$5 billion to C$8 billion ($3.6 billion to $5.8 billion) over five years, starting in 1997.
The electricity generated by the seven nuclear units will be replaced by firing up existing fossil-fuel plants at Nanticoke and Lambton at higher levels and bring back two mothballed oil-fired units.
Naticoke's eight units have a total generating capacity of 4,000 MW, while Lambton's four units total 2,000 MW.
Two 500 MW units at the Lennox generating station will be reactivated.
